title: Numbers 3: One Pair (одни with plural-only nouns)
titleRussian: Числа 3: одна пара (одни со словами только во множественном)
description: A small group of Russian nouns has no singular form: часы (watch), джинсы (jeans), очки (glasses), ножницы (scissors). With these, 'one' takes a fourth form: одни. A short, focused lesson on this single use.
descriptionRussian: У некоторых русских существительных нет единственного числа: часы, джинсы, очки, ножницы. С ними 'один' принимает четвёртую форму — одни. Короткий и узкий урок.
intro: A short lesson about a small problem. Some Russian nouns have no singular at all: a watch, a pair of glasses, a pair of trousers. You met them in the first book of this level, where they had no plural rule to follow. Here they need a form of 'one' that exists for nothing else in the language. It is a corner of Russian, but the words in that corner are ones you own and use daily.
rules: A few common Russian nouns exist only in the plural: часы, джинсы, очки, ножницы, брюки. They have no singular dictionary form.
With these plural-only nouns, the number one takes a fourth form: одни.
Used in this slot, одни translates as 'one' or 'one pair of', depending on the object: одни часы (one watch), одни очки (one pair of glasses).
The three singular forms (один / одна / одно) only fit singular nouns. The form одни only fits plural-only nouns.
Counting plural-only nouns with numbers higher than one uses a different system involving the word пара ('pair'); that is left for a later track.
examples: У меня одни часы. (I have one watch.) Часы is plural-only.
У Антона одни джинсы. (Anton has one pair of jeans.) Джинсы is plural-only.
У Лены одни очки. (Lena has one pair of glasses.) Очки is plural-only.
На столе одни ножницы. (There is one pair of scissors on the table.) Ножницы is plural-only.
У меня одни брюки. (I have one pair of trousers.) Брюки is plural-only.
У Маши одна сумка. (Masha has one bag.) Сумка is regular singular: feminine, so одна, not одни.

items.promptEnglish: Recap from Lesson 2: I have one sister.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 2. Сестра is feminine, so the form is 'одна'. Today's lesson adds the fourth form, 'одни', for nouns that have no singular at all.

items.hint: Часы has no singular form. Which form of one matches a plural-only noun?
items.explanation: Часы is a plural-only noun. The form of one that matches a plural-only noun is 'одни'. The same applies to одни джинсы, одни очки, одни ножницы.

items.promptEnglish: Anton has one pair of jeans.
items.explanation: Джинсы is plural-only, so the form is 'одни'. English needs the helper 'pair of' here; Russian just lets the plural noun do the work, with одни in front.

items.promptEnglish: Lena has one pair of glasses.
items.explanation: Очки ends in -и and exists only in the plural, so the form is 'одни'. Russian does not have a singular *очк.

items.promptEnglish: There is one book on the table.
items.hint: Книга is a regular feminine singular noun.
items.explanation: Книга is a regular singular feminine noun. The form is 'одна', not 'одни'. Today's lesson adds the form 'одни' only for nouns that have no singular at all.

items.promptEnglish: There is one pair of scissors in the bag.
items.explanation: Ножницы is plural-only, so the form is 'одни'. The agreement story for the number one is now complete: four forms in total, three for singular nouns and one for plural-only nouns.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Брюки is plural-only. The form of one that matches a plural-only noun is 'одни'. Same pattern as одни джинсы, одни часы.

minimalPairs.explanation: Часы is plural-only, so the form of one is 'одни'. 'Одна' would only fit a feminine singular noun, but часы has no singular.
Собака is a normal feminine singular noun, so the form is 'одна'. 'Одни' only fits plural-only nouns (часы, джинсы, очки).

reviewVocab.definition: plural-only noun (часы, джинсы, очки, ножницы, брюки; has no singular form)
reviewVocab.example: Слово 'часы' — существительное только во множественном числе: формы 'час' в этом значении просто нет.

reviewVocab.definition: the fourth form of 'one', used with plural-only nouns
reviewVocab.example: Говорим 'одни джинсы', потому что 'джинсы' — существительное только во множественном числе.

reviewVocab.definition: pair (used to count plural-only nouns above one: две пары джинсов; the full counting system is left for a later track)
reviewVocab.example: Для чисел больше одного с такими существительными часто используют слово 'пара': 'две пары очков'.
